t.E515.agn: In 2019, EFSA re-evaluated sulphuric acid and its sodium, potassium, calcium and ammonium salts together; it decided that a numerical ADI was not necessary and that there was no safety concern at the reported use levels (in 1991 the SCF had set the group ADI as 'not specified'). A laxative (diarrhoea-inducing) effect has been reported in humans at sodium sulphate doses of 300 mg/kg body weight and above; the estimated intake from the food additive is far below this dose.
t.E515.body: Sulphate is absorbed from the digestive tract, distributes freely in the blood, does not accumulate in tissues and is excreted mostly via the kidneys; at high doses it is also excreted in faeces.
t.E515.eff.0.a: 300 mg of sodium sulphate or more per kilogram of body weight
t.E515.eff.0.t: A laxative (diarrhoea-inducing) effect has been reported; the estimated intake from the additive is far below this dose
t.E515.found.0: May be used at quantum satis (as much as needed) in many foods in the EU
t.E515.prod: It may be obtained from natural mineral deposits or by chemical production.
t.E515.regx.0: Sulphuric acid and its sulphates (E 513–E 517) re-evaluated together; no safety concern, no numerical ADI needed.
t.E515.regx.1: Group I additive (potassium sulphates); permitted at quantum satis.
t.E515.summary: Potassium sulphates. Used in salt substitute blends.
t.E515.what: Potassium sulphate and potassium hydrogen sulphate, used as acidity regulators.
